messages:
Martin (Acme): Hey team — since yesterday afternoon our embeddings calls to /v1/embeddings have huge tail latency spikes (p95 ~1.8s, p99 ~3.4s) and intermittently return a dimension error: "EmbeddingDimensionMismatch: expected 1536 got 768". We rolled a change to dynamic batching parameters last night (see config below). Any ideas?

Sam L: Sorry you're hitting that, Martin. Can you paste the request example + the exact client model id you're calling? Also share the batching config you changed.

Martin (Acme): Example request (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "open-embed-1536-v2",
  "input": ["short text 1", "short text 2", ...]
}
```
Batching config we changed in Dedicated pool UI at ~2026-03-02 22:10:
```
{ "dynamic_batching": true,
  "max_batch_size": 128,
  "coalesce_window_ms": 50,
  "batch_timeout_ms": 30
}
```
We also started seeing a bunch of mixed-size requests — some clients send single short strings, others send 256-long docs.

redwood-bot: Noted. Ticket #SUP-12345 created and assigned to Sam L & Priya R.

Sam L: Thanks. Two immediate hypotheses: (1) the dimension mismatch suggests some requests are routed to a different model variant (768-dim) — perhaps client is sending older model id or we auto-fell back to a compact variant. (2) dynamic batching + high variance in request lengths can cause tail latency due to padding or large-request blocking.

Sam L: Quick ask: can you run one of the failing requests with the debug header and paste the invocation id? e.g., `X-Request-Debug: true` so we can surface routing logs.

Martin (Acme): Got an invocation id: inv_20260302_abc123. Also attaching a small log snippet from our side showing the long latency: 
```
[2026-03-02T22:37:12Z] request_id=inv_20260302_abc123 duration_ms=1834 status=200 model=open-embed-1536-v2 tokens=12
[2026-03-02T22:40:05Z] request_id=inv_20260302_def456 duration_ms=3401 status=500 error=EmbeddingDimensionMismatch expected=1536 got=768 model=open-embed-1536-v2
```

Priya R: Thanks. I pulled routing logs for inv_20260302_def456 — it shows that request was routed to node pool 'dedicated-gpu-B' which hosts both open-embed-1536-v2 and a cached 768-dim variant (open-embed-768-quant). Fallback logic kicked in because the primary replica was overloaded and we attempted to route to a compatible variant but failed dimension validation.

Priya R: On tail latency: I can see frequent interleaving of very-small (1-3 tokens) requests and very-large (>>1024 tokens) requests in the same batch. With max_batch_size=128 and coalesce_window_ms=50 we end up waiting to fill the batch then padding large items, which both increases per-token overhead and creates blocking. Also large requests occasionally exceed per-shard token limits triggering slower exec paths.

Jia W: Repro suggestion: Martin, can you run a small script that sends 1000 requests with same model id but two sizes interleaved (1 token / 2048 tokens) and capture p50/p95/p99? That will reproduce the starved small-request tail behavior. Example python snippet:
```
for i in range(1000):
  text = "short" if i % 2 == 0 else "long" * 2048
  client.embeddings.create(model="open-embed-1536-v2", input=[text])
```

Martin (Acme): Will try. We can repro locally and see same spike.

Sam L: Mitigations while we investigate:
- Temporarily set max_batch_size to 64 to reduce large-request blocking.
- Reduce coalesce_window_ms to 10ms so small requests don't wait as long to fill batches.
- Set a per-route max_request_tokens or max_batch_token_budget to prevent huge docs from joining mixed batches.
- Pin critical clients to a low-latency pool (create a separate dedicated pool or use priority tags).

Sam L: Also, please confirm all clients are calling the correct model id. If some clients still call legacy 768-dim model, that explains the mismatch. We can also disable auto-fallback to the 768 variant temporarily.

Priya R: I'll open a short-lived guard: disable cross-variant fallback on 'dedicated-gpu-B' to prevent auto-routing to 768 until the pool is stable. That should eliminate dimension mismatch errors.

Martin (Acme): We confirmed one internal service was still pointing at `open-embed-768-v1` — fixing that now. After the fix, we'll run the repro script and report back.

redwood-bot: Action log: disabled-fallback on dedicated-gpu-B (by Priya R) at 2026-03-02T23:05:00Z.

Martin (Acme): Quick follow-up: after disabling fallback and reducing max_batch_size to 64, p95 dropped to ~420ms and p99 to ~880ms in our smoke tests. Looks much better.

Jia W: Great. For longer-term: we recommend tuning batching along these lines:
- Prefer token-aware batching (max_batch_tokens) over pure `max_batch_size` when request lengths vary widely.
- Set a `priority_tag` for small-latency-critical clients to avoid coalescing with large docs.
- Use model variant pinning to avoid cross-variant fallbacks (especially when dims differ).
- Run periodic evals where workload mixes different doc sizes to detect regressions.

Sam L: We'll keep ticket SUP-12345 open for a week to monitor. Priya/R will roll a small autoscaler tweak to reduce thrash on that pool overnight. Jia, can you add a short note in the docs about token-aware batching heuristics?

Jia W: On it. I'll add a snippet to the batching troubleshooting doc with recommended defaults.

Martin (Acme): Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick help. We'll ping if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:

Sam L: Thanks Martin — assigning follow-ups: Priya — pool autoscaler tweak; Jia — docs; Sam — confirm rollback guard remains for 24h. Marking as monitored on ticket SUP-12345. :white_check_mark:
